Priror to the PCA visualization varied bash scripts were used on an HPCC cluster to process data.

The PCA is from the PLINK PCA function after snps were genotyped with GATK and filtered with BCF Tools. 

PCA Visualization
```{r}
#Defining Labels and Colors
```

```{r}
#code generated with ai assistance for optimization
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#I manually downloaded the files from the HPCC
eVector <- read_table("BWA_Out_quick.g.vcf.gz_pca.eigenvec", col_names = FALSE)
# Name columns: FID IID PC1..PC10
colnames(eVector) <- c("FID","IID", paste0("PC", 1: (ncol(eVector)-2)))
# Read eigenvalues and compute % variance
eValues <- read_table("BWA_Out_quick.g.vcf.gz_pca.eigenval", col_names = FALSE)[[1]]
var_pct <- 100 * eValues / sum(eValues)
pc1_lab <- sprintf("PC1 (%.2f%%)", var_pct[1])
pc2_lab <- sprintf("PC2 (%.2f%%)", var_pct[2])
#population IDs Clean
Pops <- read_csv("UpdatedSampleIDs.csv")
eVector <- eVector %>% left_join(Pops, by = "FID")
# Optional: join metadata (CSV with columns IID, Group, etc.)
# meta <- read.csv("sample_metadata.csv")
# evec <- evec %>% left_join(meta, by = "IID")

gg <- ggplot(eVector, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Pop), size = 2.2) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA: PC1 vs PC2",
    x = pc1_lab,
    y = pc2_lab,
    color = "Population"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pop_colors,
    labels = pop_labels,
    name = "Population"
  )
print(gg)
#ggsave("TM_PC11_PC12.png", gg, width = 6.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)

# Add labels (optional)
# gg + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = IID), size = 3)

```



Scree Plot
```{r}
#code generated with ai assistance for optimization
#need to run above chunk first
k <- min(13, length(var_pct))

scree <- data.frame(PC = factor(1:k), VarPct = var_pct[1:k])

s_gg <- ggplot(scree, aes(x = PC, y = VarPct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C72B0") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", VarPct)), vjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(title = "PCA Scree Plot", x = "Principal component", y = "Variance explained (%)")
print(s_gg)
ggsave("TM_scree.png", s_gg, width = 6.5, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```

```{r Stats Check, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
#anovas are the most appropriate so that we can do a Tukey
#Making Anova models first
PC1_anova <- aov(PC1 ~ Pop, data = eVector)
PC1_check <- summary(PC1_anova)
print(PC1_check)
PC2_anova <- aov(PC2 ~ Pop, data = eVector)
PC2_check <- summary(PC2_anova)
print(PC2_check)
#Run Tukey Test
tukey_PC1 <- TukeyHSD(PC1_anova)
print(tukey_PC1)
tukey_PC2 <- TukeyHSD(PC2_anova)
print(tukey_PC2)
#View Tukey
plot(tukey_PC1)
plot(tukey_PC2)
```

```{bash}
#writing the bash script notes before putting into text edit
#code generated with ai assistance for optimization
#the commands
#Define variables
VCF=$1
IDs=$2
#this needed to be fixed
BASENAME= (basename * .vcf.gz)
NEW_VCF="${BASENAME}_read.vcf"
#this is pi per window
#window = 0 is whole genome
#Easiest
pixy --vcf "${VCF}" \
     --populations "${IDs}" \
     --stats pi \
     --window-size 50000 \
     --n_cores 8 \
     --output_prefix pixy_overall

#annotating stuff
#genome_db??
snpEff ann -v your_genome_db "${VCF}" > "${NEW_VCF}"

#find synonmyous sites
#this overwrites everyrun
grep -E "synonymous_variant" "${NEW_VCF}" | \
   awk '{print $1":"$2}' > syn_sites.txt

#nonsynonmous sites
#this overwrites everyrun
grep -E "missense_variant|nonsense_variant" "${NEW_VCF}" | \
   awk '{print $1":"$2}' > nonsyn_sites.txt

#Now Run Pixy again
#synonmous
pixy --vcf "${NEW_VCF}" \
     --populations "${IDs}" \
     --stats pi \
     --site-file syn_sites.txt \
     --output_prefix pixy_syn
#nonsynonmous
pixy --vcf "${NEW_VCF}" \
     --populations "${IDs}" \
     --stats pi \
     --site-file nonsyn_sites.txt \
     --output_prefix pixy_nonsyn


#I think this is how to do Hz
vcftools --vcf "${VCF}" \
         --het \
         --out het_out

vcftools --vcf "${VCF}" --het 
vcftools --positions syn_sites.txt --het
vcftools --positions nonsyn_sites.txt --het

```

It seems when I did Bowtie I over filtered

Bowtiescript used

```{bash}

#!/bin/bash --login
#SBATCH --job-name=BowtieArray
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/%x_%A_%a.err
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --array=0-12    # you will override with sbatch --array=


#cleaned up and simpllified assistance from AI - Copilot 

set -euo pipefail

# ------------------------------
# INPUT VARIABLES
# ------------------------------
        # directory of fastq files

module purge
module load Bowtie2 
module load SAMtools 


REF="$1"                        # reference fasta
READS="${2:-./READS}"  
BowOut="${3:-./BowtieOut}"      # output directory
THREADS="${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}"

mkdir -p "$BowOut" logs

# ------------------------------
# FIND R1 AND R2 FILES
# ------------------------------
mapfile -t R1_FILES < <(find "$READS" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -iname "*R1*.fastq" -o -iname "*R1*.fastq.gz" \) | sort)

mapfile -t R2_FILES < <(find "$READS" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -iname "*R2*.fastq" -o -iname "*R2*.fastq.gz" \) | sort)

# ------------------------------
# STRIP READ MARKER TO CREATE PAIRING KEYS
# ------------------------------
strip_read_marker() {
  local f="$1"
  local base
  base="$(basename "$f")"
  base="${base%.fastq}"
  base="${base%.fastq.gz}"
  base="$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/([._-])R[12]([._-]|$)/\1SAMPLE\2/')"
  base="$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/([._-])001([._-]|$)/\1\2/')"
  echo "$base"
}

# ------------------------------
# BUILD MAPPING FOR R1 → sample key and R2 → same sample key
# ------------------------------
declare -A MAP_R1 MAP_R2

for f in "${R1_FILES[@]}"; do
  k="$(strip_read_marker "$f")"
  MAP_R1["$k"]="$f"
done
for f in "${R2_FILES[@]}"; do
  k="$(strip_read_marker "$f")"
  MAP_R2["$k"]="$f"
done

# ------------------------------
# CREATE ORDERED LIST OF PAIRED SAMPLES
# ------------------------------
pairs=()
while IFS= read -r key; do
  if [[ -n "${MAP_R1[$key]:-}" && -n "${MAP_R2[$key]:-}" ]]; then
    pairs+=("$key")
  fi
done < <(printf "%s\n" "${!MAP_R1[@]}" | sort)

NUM_PAIRS="${#pairs[@]}"

# ------------------------------
# SELECT SAMPLE FOR THIS ARRAY INDEX
# ------------------------------
IDX="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}"
KEY="${pairs[$IDX]}"
R1="${MAP_R1[$KEY]}"
R2="${MAP_R2[$KEY]}"
SAMPLE="$(basename "$KEY" | sed -E 's/SAMPLE//g' | sed -E 's/[._-]+$//')"

echo "=== Running sample $SAMPLE ==="
echo "R1 = $R1"
echo "R2 = $R2"


REF_INDEX="$REF"

echo "Using existing Bowtie2 index:"
echo "  Prefix: $REF_INDEX"
echo "  Expected files:"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.1.bt2"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.2.bt2"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.3.bt2"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.4.bt2"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.rev.1.bt2"
echo "    ${REF_INDEX}.rev.2.bt2"


# ------------------------------
# ALIGN + SORT BAM
# ------------------------------
bam_out="${BowOut}/${SAMPLE}.bam"

echo "==> Aligning $SAMPLE → ${bam_out}"
bowtie2 \
    -p "$THREADS" \
    -x "$REF_INDEX" \
    -1 "$R1" \
    -2 "$R2" \
  | samtools view -b - \
  | samtools sort -@ "$THREADS" -o "$bam_out"

echo "==> Finished sample: $SAMPLE"
```
